purpose: Deterministically flatten every parsed MIDI note event onto one piano-key timeline before notation reconstruction.

semanticBoundary.output: one synthetic global piano-roll source part

retentionPolicy.zeroDuration: preserve through reduction unless merged into a positive-duration duplicate; existing downstream zero-duration policy remains authoritative

duplicatePolicy.key: canonical onset unit + MIDI note number
duplicatePolicy.velocity: maximum contributor velocity for deterministic compatibility
duplicatePolicy.contributors: retain as provenance/diagnostic metadata where representable
duplicatePolicy.purpose: remove duplicate key attacks only; do not perform arrangement, simplification, melody extraction, or instrument prioritization

nonNoteMidiPolicy.programChange: metadata only; does not remove notes
nonNoteMidiPolicy.trackName: metadata only; does not remove notes
nonNoteMidiPolicy.channel: provenance only; does not remove notes
nonNoteMidiPolicy.pitchBend: underlying note event is retained at its discrete MIDI note number; pitch-bend metadata must not reject or remove the note in this piano-roll profile
nonNoteMidiPolicy.controllers: do not create or remove piano-key attacks unless a separately frozen semantic rule is introduced

ordering.stage: after raw MIDI parse and canonical onset projection, before instrument-based classification and before notation/polyphony/rhythm reconstruction
ordering.oldH1NonPitchedFiltering: superseded for this production MIDI-to-Braille profile; H1 parser fact capture remains valid
ordering.tripletProvenance: must be re-audited after reduction implementation

scalability.requirement: the production implementation must not build one unbounded whole-song combinatorial rhythm/polyphony solve merely because all notes share one output part
scalability.processingBoundary: notation/rhythm solving must remain bounded by musical measure and/or small connected constraint component
scalability.reason: the first whole-source simulation became CPU-bound on Oxygene after flattening; the lightweight reduction itself completed quickly

userGuidance.shortWarning: All MIDI tracks and channels are merged into one piano roll. Nothing is removed automatically. Remove any unwanted material before importing.
userGuidance.fullGuide: The MIDI converter performs a deterministic piano-roll reduction. All MIDI tracks, channels, and instruments are placed onto one shared musical timeline and treated as keys of a single piano. The converter does not classify or remove percussion, sound effects, or other instruments. If the source MIDI contains material that should not appear in the piano reduction, remove it before conversion. No musical material is removed for arrangement or simplification. Only duplicate attacks with the same canonical onset and MIDI pitch are collapsed; the longest contributor release is retained.

nonGoals: dropping notes because of program/channel classification
implementationSequence: introduce explicit global piano-roll reducer after raw parse
route production MIDI translation through reducer before old classification
retain all note events irrespective of channel/program
collapse duplicate canonical-onset+pitch attacks with max-end policy
make pitch bend non-destructive for this reduction profile
keep notation solving bounded by measure/component
run real-world smoke on all four SHA-pinned MIDI files
re-run triplet provenance audit on the reduced representation
only then design the triplet fix
